ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p379/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p379/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p379/r3.claim: Ibn Abd Allah and Talha read yubdiʾ with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl; most read the latter open.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p379/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وطلحة: يبدىء، بضم الياء وكسر الدال والجمهور: بفتحها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p379/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p379/r4.speaker: الأبوان والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p379/r4.claim: The two readers use third-person yarjiʿūn, while most address the audience as tarjiʿūn, meaning return to God's reward or punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p379/r4.anchor: والأبوان: يرجعون، بياء الغيبة والجمهور: بتاء الخطاب، أي إلى ثوابه وعقابه

ASAD-NOTES:30:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:intro/r2.claim: Its central theme is God's creation, bringing life from death, and power and promise to resurrect the dead.
ASAD-NOTES:30:intro/r2.anchor: the wonder of God's creation of all that exists

STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r8.claim: The discussion turns from the disbelievers’ failure to reflect to the different ends of believers and disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r8.anchor: the sūrah proceeds to a discussion of the disparate ends of believers and disbelievers (vv. 10–16)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p17/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p17/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p17/r2.claim: God will sift sincere believers from hypocrites; the believers are sincere followers, unlike claimants unwilling to face hardship, and justice requires this distinction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p17/r2.anchor: If He does not do this, it will be against His justice.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r1.claim: The verse claims that God will recreate humanity and offers His initiation of creation as evidence for that claim.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r1.anchor: Found in these few words are both the claim and the evidence to this claim.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r2.claim: Re-creation is no harder than initial creation; indeed, repeating a task is easier, answering the deniers' claim that resurrection is far-fetched.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r2.anchor: repeating a task is easier than doing it for the first time.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r3.claim: Everyone returns to God alone, countering the polytheists' belief that they would return to favored deities who could intercede for them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p67/r3.anchor: Every one will return to God alone and no one else on that day will be there to which they will return.

RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r1.claim: Since the preceding account of their fate mentions Hell, it implies resurrection; al-Razi says God does not leave that claim without proof.
RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r1.anchor: لما ذكر أن عاقبتهم إلى الجحيم وكان في ذلك إشارة إلى الإعادة والحشر

RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r2.claim: The one who created by power and will is able to bring creation back, so the resurrection claim is demonstrated and return is to God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r2.anchor: يعني من خلق بالقدرة والإرادة لا يعجز عن الرجعة والإعادة فإليه ترجعون

RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p89#2/r3.claim: The following verse then describes what happens when people return to God.

BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r1.claim: Al-Shafi'i says engaging in kalam leads to heresy; the burden of this bad innovation and of those who imitate it is recorded for its originator until Resurrection, without reducing their burdens.
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r1.anchor: وقد قال الشافعي رحمه الله : من تكلم تزندق ثم وبال هذه جملة إلى قيام الساعة

BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r2.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r2.claim: Al-Tawilat al-Najmiyya condemns those who deny the Quran and call prophets bearers of laws and the revealed laws the greatest law, invoking repeated curses upon them.
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r2.anchor: كذبوا بالقرآن وسموا الأنبياء عليهم السلام أصحاب النواميس وسموا الشرائع الناموس الأكبر عليهم لعنات الله تترى كذا في "تأويلات" حضرة الشيخ نجم الدين

BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r3.claim: God first creates people in worldly life, specifically the human from a drop of fluid, then revives and raises them after death in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r3.anchor: يخلقهم أولا في الدنيا وهو الإنسان المخلوق من النطفة

BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r4.claim: They return only to God's place of reckoning and recompense; the shift to direct address intensifies the warning.
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r4.anchor: {ثم إليه} أي : إلى موقف حسابه تعالى وجزائه

BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r5.claim: A variant reads the verb in third-person plural, they return, following the collective meaning of khalq.
BURSEVI:v7p7#2/r5.anchor: وقرىء بياء الغيبة والجمع باعتبار معنى الخلق

STUDYQURAN:30:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:11/r1.claim: One reading is that God first composes human beings from dust and then resurrects them.
STUDYQURAN:30:11/r1.anchor: the composition of human beings from dust and their resurrection

STUDYQURAN:30:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:11/r2.claim: Alternatively, the phrase concerns the beginning of all creation and the eventual return of all things to God.
STUDYQURAN:30:11/r2.anchor: the beginning of all creation and the eventual return of all things to God

STUDYQURAN:30:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:11/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:11/r3.claim: The return to God refers to the Resurrection and the return of all things to Him.
STUDYQURAN:30:11/r3.anchor: Then unto Him shall you be returned (cf. 2:28, 245; 10:56; 11:34; 21:35

TAB-FULL:v18p468/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p468/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p468/r1.claim: God alone initiates all creation without partner or helper, bringing it into existence from nothing by His power.
TAB-FULL:v18p468/r1.anchor: ولم يك شيئا {ثم إليه ترجعون} [البقرة: 28] يقول: ثم إليه من بعد إعادتهم

TAB-FULL:v18p468/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p468/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p468/r2.claim: After annihilating creation, God recreates it as a new creation, just as He first made it complete from nothing.
TAB-FULL:v18p468/r2.anchor: ثم إليه من بعد إعادتهم خلقا جديدا يردون، فيحشرون لفصل القضاء بينهم

TAB-FULL:v18p468/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p468/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p468/r3.claim: After resurrection people return to God, are gathered for judgment, and are recompensed for their deeds.
TAB-FULL:v18p468/r3.anchor: {ثم إليه ترجعون} [البقرة: 28] يقول: ثم إليه من بعد إعادتهم خلقا جديدا يردون، فيحشرون

TABATABAI:30:9-12/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:9-12/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:9-12/r10.claim: The verse summarizes the proof: God originates and repeats creation, and all creatures return to Him; the plural return pronoun refers to the created beings.
TABATABAI:30:9-12/r10.anchor: بعد ما ذكر الحجة وتكذيب كثير من الناس لخص القول في نتيجتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r1.claim: Muqātil says God first created people, then will restore them alive after death as they were; they return to Him for recompense according to their deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: الله بدأ خلق الناس فخلقهم أولا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r2.claim: The final verb is read with yāʾ or tāʾ. The yāʾ form follows preceding third-person wording; plural رجوعون follows خلق in meaning while يعيده follows its singular form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r2.anchor: فمن قرأ بالياء فلأن المتقدم ذكره غيبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r3.claim: The yāʾ reading follows the plural sense of خلق, whereas يعيده follows the word’s singular form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r3.anchor: وجاء قوله: (ثم يعيده) على لفظ الخلق، وقوله: (ترجعون) على المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r4.claim: The tāʾ reading shifts from third-person narration to direct address, as in the transition between 1:2 and 1:5.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p24/r4.anchor: ووجه التاء أنه صار من الغيبة إلى الخطاب، ونظيره: {الحمد لله رب العالمين}

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p647#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p647#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p647#2/r6.claim: God’s bringing creation back means resurrection; people return to Him on Judgment Day.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p647#2/r6.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده} [الروم: 11] ، يعني: البعث {ثم إليه ترجعون} [الروم: 11] يوم القيامة.

QASHANI:30:11-14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:30:11-14/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:30:11-14/r1.claim: God begins creation by making the Persians prevail over the Romans and restores it by making the Romans prevail over the Persians; return to Him is annihilation in Him.
QASHANI:30:11-14/r1.anchor: { الله يبدأ الخلق } بإظهار الفرس على الروم { ثم يعيده } بإظهار الروم على الفرس { ثم إليه ترجعون } بالفناء فيه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r1.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r1.claim: God independently brought all creatures into being by his unique power, without partners, helpers, or prior material, and can recreate them after destroying them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r1.anchor: sırf kendi eşsiz kudretiyle baştan inşa ettiği, bunları yok ettikten sonra da tekrar aynı şekilde yaratma gücüne sahip olduğu belirtilmektedir (Taberî, XXI, 25)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r2.claim: The repeated creation may refer to nature’s continual renewal by God, resurrection after the Day of Judgment, or both.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r2.anchor: Yaratmanın tekrar edilmesi ifadesiyle, tabiattaki sürekli yenilenmenin yine yüce Allah’ın irade ve kudretiyle gerçekleştiğine veya kıyamet sonrası dirilişe ya da bunların her ikisine işaret edilmiş olabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r3.claim: These events invite reflection on the wisdom of creation and recreation and remind people that appearing before God for judgment is inevitable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:11/r3.anchor: bunlara değinilmesindeki asıl amaç, insanın, yaratılış ve yeniden yaratılışla ilgili bütün bu gelişmelerin hikmeti üzerinde düşünmesini sağlamak ve sonunda mutlak kemal sahibi Allah’ın huzuruna çıkarılıp hesap vermenin kaçınılmaz olduğunu hatırlatmaktır

ITQAN:v2p551/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p551/r3.speaker: الجرجاني
ITQAN:v2p551/r3.claim: Al-Jurjani allows the pronoun of separation before an imperfect verb and applies it to the phrase huwa yubdiʾu wa-yuʿid; Abu al-Baqa applies it similarly to a second example.
ITQAN:v2p551/r3.anchor: وجوز الجرجاني وقوعه قبل مضارع وجعل منه ﴿ إنه هو يبدئ ويعيد ﴾ وجعل منه أبو البقاء

ASAD-NOTES:30:11#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:30:11#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:30:11#n9/r1.claim: God brings human beings forth anew; Asad links this to 10:4 and notes a more general formulation at 30:27.
ASAD-NOTES:30:11#n9/r1.anchor: cf. 10:4 and the corresponding note 8. (A more general formulation of the same statement is found in verse 27 of this surah.)

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r1.claim: Abu Amr and Abu Bakr's transmission from Asim read يرجعون with yāʾ; Ibn Abbas also reports the tāʾ form from Abu Amr.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r1.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو، وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر: (ثم إليه يرجعون) بالياء [الروم/ 11]

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r2.claim: These readers use the second-person form ترجعون with tāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم ترجعون بالتاء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r3.claim: The yāʾ continues third-person narration and follows the plural sense of الخلق; the tāʾ reading shifts to direct address, like the Fatiha.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p444#3/r3.anchor: حجة الياء أن المتقدم ذكره غيبة يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ثم إليه يرجعون

IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r4.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r4.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim and Abu Amr read يرجعون with yāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r4.anchor: فقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو ﴿ يرجعون ﴾ بالياء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r5.speaker: عياش عن أبي عمرو، وابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r5.claim: Ayash transmits ترجعون with tāʾ from Abu Amr; the named readers and Hafs from Asim also read it with tāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p506/r5.anchor: وروى عياش عن أبى عمرو ﴿ ترجعون ﴾ بالتاء

QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#1/r1.claim: A third-person plural passive changes the address from you to they and presents return as a universal cosmic principle.
QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#1/r1.anchor: Third-person masculine plural passive — shifts addressee from ""you"" to ""they,"" universalizing the return

QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#2/r1.claim: A third-person plural active means they return voluntarily, removing passive compulsion and assigning agency to the subjects.
QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#2/r1.anchor: Third-person masculine plural active — ""they return"" voluntarily, removing passive compulsion; subjects have agency

QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#3/r1.claim: The second-person plural active means you return voluntarily, preserving direct address while assigning human agency.
QIRAAT-ER:30:11:8#3/r1.anchor: Second-person masculine plural active — ""you return"" voluntarily, preserving direct address but granting human agency

ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r1.claim: God originates creation, restores it through resurrection, and all return to Him for recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r1.anchor: ثم يعيده ( بالبعث ( ثم إليه ترجعون

ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r2.speaker: عبدالله وطلحة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r2.claim: Abdullah and Talha read the verb as يبديء, with a prefixed damma and kasra on the dal.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبدالله وطلحة ( يبديء ) بضم الياء وكسر الدال

ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r3.claim: Fronting the destination conveys restriction; shifting from third-person narration to direct address confronts the polytheists with an intensified personal threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r3.anchor: وتقديم المعمول للتخصيص وكان الظاهر يرجعون بياء الغيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو وروح
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r4.claim: Abu Amr and Rawh read يرجعون in third-person plural, as expected from the surrounding narration.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p24#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وروح ( يرجعون ) بياء الغيبة كما هو الظاهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r5.claim: God first creates people and then restores them alive after death; the pronoun refers back to “creation,” rather than explicitly saying “He restores them.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r5.anchor: أي: يخلقهم ابتداء ثم يعيدهم بعد الموت أحياء، ولم يقل: يعيدهم، رده إلى الخلق، {ثم إليه ترجعون}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r6.claim: People return to God so that He may recompense them for their deeds.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو، أبو بكر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r7.claim: Abu Amr and Abu Bakr read the verb with yāʾ, “they return.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو، وأبو بكر: "يرجعون" بالياء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r8.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r8.claim: The other readers read the verb with tāʾ, “you return.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p263/r8.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو، وأبو بكر: "يرجعون" بالياء، والآخرون بالتاء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r1.claim: God originates creation and then restores it through resurrection; people return to Him for judgment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r2.claim: The shift to direct address emphasizes the intended point.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r2.anchor: والعدول إلى الخطاب للمبالغة في المقصود

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r3.speaker: أبو بكر وأبو عمرو وروح
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r3.claim: Abū Bakr, Abū ʿAmr, and Rawḥ read يرجعون in the third person, following the preceding wording.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:11-13/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر وأبو عمرو وروح بالياء على الأصل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r6.claim: Since God originates creation, He can restore it after annihilation; explicitly stating the conclusion affects the soul and recaps the preceding proof, while the ability to repeat one's own creation is self-evident.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r6.anchor: قادر على الإعادة كما قدر على الابتداءن وكان للتصريح مع النفس حالة ليست لغيره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r7.claim: God continually begins whatever creation He wills, as people observe, then restores it after it perishes.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r7.anchor: بدا منه ما رأيتم وهو يجدد في كل حين ما يريد من ذلك كما تشاهدون

BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r8.claim: People return to God alone: inwardly, all affairs belong to Him even when limited vision attributes them to causes, and bodily after the Resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r8.anchor: ثم إليه } أي لا إلى غيره { ترجعون * } معنى في أموركم كلها في الدنيا وإن كنتم لقصور النظر تنسبونها إلى الأسباب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r9.speaker: الجماعة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r9.claim: The general reading addresses the hearers directly with ترجعون; Abu Amr, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Rawh from Yaqub read يرجعون in third person, matching the preceding narrative, while direct address is more explicit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p605/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم وروح عن يعقوب بالياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r1.claim: The argument begins from what the polytheists must concede: God alone originated creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r1.anchor: استدلال بما لا يسعهم إلا الاعتراف به وهو بدء الخلق إذ لا ينازعون في أن الله وحده هو خالق الخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r2.claim: Resurrection is embedded as an a fortiori inference: whoever concedes the first creation should more readily concede its repetition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r2.anchor: إذا سلم له بدء الخلق كان تسليم إعادته أولى وأجدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r3.claim: After successive past and present nations, their fates illustrate return after death; recalling the deniers’ worldly end prepares a persuasive case for resurrection and judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r3.anchor: ناسب في مقام الاعتبار أن يقام لهم الاستدلال على إمكان البعث ليقع ذكر ما يعقبه من الجزاء موقع الإقناع لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r4.claim: Preposing the divine name before the verbal predicate serves emphasis alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r4.anchor: وتقديم اسم الجلالة على المسند الفعلي لمجرد التقوي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r5.claim: Here ثم marks rank rather than time: return to God is greater than re-creation because it is the ultimate purpose of both creation and resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r5.anchor: هنا للتراخي الرتبي كما هو شأنها في عطف الجمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r6.claim: The address to the polytheists shifts from third-person reference to direct address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r6.anchor: فالخطاب في { ترجعون } للمشركين على طريقة الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r7.speaker: الجمهور وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم وروح عن يعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p61/r7.claim: Most readers use second-person تاء ترجعون; Abu Amr, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Rawh from Yaqub read third-person ياء, matching the preceding context.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r10.claim: God proclaims universally that people will be resurrected from their graves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r10.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى إخبارا مطلقا لجميع العالم بالحشر والبعث من القبور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r11.speaker: طلحة وابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r11.claim: Ṭalḥah and Ibn Masʿūd read “yubdiʾu,” with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r11.anchor: وقرأ طلحة وابن مسعود «يبدىء» بضم الياء وكسر الدال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r12.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r12.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «ترجعون» بالتاء من فوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r13.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r13.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read with yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p330#3/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم بالياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r1.claim: God creates people first and restores them alive after death as they were.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r1.anchor: أي يخلقهم أولا ثم يعيدهم بعد الموت أحياء كما كانوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r2.claim: Their return to God means their recompense for their deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بذكر الرجوع الجزاء على الاعمال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r3.claim: These readers recite the second-person plural, shifting from report to direct address.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم ترجعون بالتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r4.claim: These readers recite the third-person plural, matching the preceding mention of people in the third person.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم بالياء لأن المتقدم ذكره غيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r5.claim: Al-khalq here means created beings, while the singular pronoun in yuʿīduhu follows the word's grammatical form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p291#2/r5.anchor: والخلق بمعنى المخلوقين وإنما قال يعيده على لفظ الخلق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p306#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p306#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p306#2/r1.claim: As God can originate creation, He can restore it; people return to Him on Judgment Day, when He repays each person according to deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p306#2/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى: {الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده} أي: كما هو قادر

JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr and some transmitters from ʿĀṣim read the verb in the third person, referring to creation.
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم في بعض الروايات: يرجعون بالياء كناية عن الخلق

JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r2.claim: The other readers use the second-person form; all agree on its ḍamma vocalization except Yaʿqūb, who opens it throughout the Qurʾān.
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r2.anchor: الباقون بالتاء على الخطاب، واتفقوا على ضمها غير يعقوب الحضرمي فإنه يفتحها في جميع القرآن

JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r5.claim: Badʾ is the beginning of an action and is the opposite of ending; it is also contrasted with returning.
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r5.anchor: البدء: أول الفعل، بدأ يبدأ، وابتدأ ابتداء، والابتداء: نقيض الانتهاء، والبدء نقيض العود

JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r6.claim: Repetition is doing something a second time; applying return to speech is figurative, while it is literal for bodies and enduring accidents, not sounds.
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r6.anchor: والإعادة: فعل الشيء ثانية، وإذا قيل: عاد الكلام فهو على التقدير، إلا أنه توسع فيه، حقيقة في الأجسام

JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r7.claim: Restoration, return, and second creation are equivalent terms, and God alone can restore after annihilation.
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r7.anchor: والإعادة والرجعة والنشأة الثانية نظائر، أعاد يعيد إعادة، والله تعالى المختص بالقدرة على الإعادة بعد الإفناء

JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r8.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r8.claim: The Qāḍī gives three conditions for restoration: the thing can persist, is not generated, and lies within the Creator’s power.
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r8.anchor: وثالثها: أن يكون من مقدور القديم سبحانه، عن القاضي.

JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r9.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī’s three conditions are that it is within God’s exclusive power, can persist, and is of a kind only God can restore.
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r9.anchor: ومما يبقى يكون جنسه مقدرا للقدر، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r10.claim: Another formulation requires that the thing be within God’s power, can persist, and is not generated from a cause that does not persist.
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: ثلاثة أشياء: أن يكون مقدورا للقديم، ومما يبقى، وألا يكون متولدا من سببه لايبقى

JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r11.claim: Reason requires restoring the rewarded and anyone owed compensation not paid in this life; punishment is God’s right and could be omitted, but revelation promises restoration of every living accountable or unaccountable being.
JISHUMI:v8p5604#2/r11.anchor: قلنا: أما في العقل: يجب إعادة المثاب ومن له عوض لم يوفر عليه في الدنيا، فأما المعاقب فهو حق لله تعالى

JISHUMI:v8p5608/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r2.claim: The statement that God restores creation supports the author’s position that annihilation precedes restoration, since restoration requires prior annihilation.
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r2.anchor: يدل قوله: (ثم يعيده) على صحة قولنا في الفناء والإعادة؛ لأن الإعادة إنما تصح إذا صح الفناء

JISHUMI:v8p5608/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r3.speaker: أبو علي، وأبو هاشم، وأصحابهما
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī, Abū Hāshim, and their followers say God creates an opposite called annihilation, while bodies and their accidents remain.
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r3.anchor: عن أبي علي، وأبي هاشم، وأصحابهما. وقيل: بل يعدم الأجسام

JISHUMI:v8p5608/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r4.speaker: أبو الحسين الخياط
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r4.claim: Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Khayyāṭ says that bodies themselves are annihilated.
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r4.anchor: وقيل: بل يعدم الأجسام، عن أبي الحسين الخياط

JISHUMI:v8p5608/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r5.claim: A further view says God creates in bodies a state that does not endure and creates no subsequent state, so they cease to exist.
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r5.anchor: وقيل: بل يخلق فيها كونا لا يبقى، ولا يخلق عقيبه كونا آخر، فينتفي

JISHUMI:v8p5608/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r6.speaker: الجاحظ
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r6.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ says bodies do not perish; God restores them by gathering and reviving them.
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r6.anchor: وقيل: لا تفنى الأجسام؛ وإنما يعيدها بأن يجمعها ويحييها، عن الجاحظ

JISHUMI:v8p5608/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r7.claim: The claim that God simply says “perish” and the bodies perish is a weak argument.
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r7.anchor: وقيل: يقول: افن، فيفنى، وهذا ركيك من القول

JISHUMI:v8p5608/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r8.claim: The return to God establishes resurrection.
JISHUMI:v8p5608/r8.anchor: ويدل قوله: (ثم إليه ترجعون) على إثبات المعاد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p476/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p476/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p476/r1.claim: Returning to God means returning to His reward or punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p476/r1.anchor: ثم إليه ترجعون } أي إلى ثوابه وعقابه .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p476/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p476/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p476/r2.claim: The verb is also read in the second person with tāʾ or in the third person with yāʾ.

MUQATIL:30:11-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:30:11-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:30:11-15/r1.claim: God created people and will recreate them alive after death; they return to Him for recompense according to their deeds.
MUQATIL:30:11-15/r1.anchor: يقول: الله بدأ الناس فخلقهم، ثم يعيدهم فى الآخرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p269#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p269#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p269#2/r1.claim: God originates creation by bringing created beings into existence.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p269#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p269#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p269#2/r2.claim: God restores creation by reviving people after death.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p269#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p269#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو وسهل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p269#2/r3.claim: Abu Amr and Sahl read the verb with yāʾ rather than tāʾ.
